A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMMA and contain readable main text and Appendices A-D. Inspection of all pages, including rendered figures and tables, supports matching retained, relocated, added and omitted material.

before.justification: V2 reports original multimodal-agent and human-solver puzzle evaluations, including performance tables, conversation analyses and privacy results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds reasoning-model evaluations, information-access ablations and token-efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: The main Solver/Expert architecture, communication mechanism, memory structure, action execution and Appendix D prompts remain unchanged. Memory removal and full-information single-agent operation are introduced as experimental ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten puzzles across four capability categories, including PAD-UFES-20-based Telehealth and ATM privacy tasks. New model evaluations and information-access controls reuse this coverage; expanded Telehealth instructions do not establish a changed task.

E2.justification: V3 adds o4-mini, R1-OneVision and LLaVA-CoT to Table 1 and Appendix C while retaining the earlier comparator set. Human and o4-mini results also extend the conversation-length and privacy comparisons. Human + GPT-4o matches the earlier Human baseline.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a token-efficiency metric, temperature 0.6 for reasoning models, and memory-removal and full-information single-agent controls. Captions specify 30 puzzle initializations for o4-mini. The existing ten-turn, three-mistake limits and other models' main evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct memory and information-asymmetry ablations (Table 2), token-efficiency analysis (Figure 5), and a full Gemini failure trajectory (Appendix A, Figure 6). Existing failure, privacy and conversation-length analyses are extended. V2's capability-group performance analysis and Figure 6 are removed.

E5.justification: V3 adds model-specific run-count information specifying 30 independent o4-mini puzzle initializations, alongside the retained 100 other-AI and ten human counts. Standard-error reporting already existed and continues; no new repeated-seed protocol or significance test is documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds reasoning-model scores, ablation outcomes, efficiency scores and further failure/privacy findings, while removing capability-group results. Retained comparator table values are unchanged. The newly reported o4-mini overall PSR is 53.98%, although its displayed puzzle scores average 43.8%, leaving aggregation unclear.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a mathematical definition of conciseness from token usage and defines efficiency as its harmonic mean with PSR (Equation 1). Neither version provides a broader theoretical development or formal proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a benchmark for communication between multimodal agents with complementary information. V3's abstract and conclusion specifically emphasize reasoning-model communication failures, replacing the earlier abstract's emphasis on human involvement, and the conclusion foregrounds efficiency evaluation.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning independent reasoning versus communication, token efficiency, memory dependence and task-specific benefits of collaboration. Section 7 substantially expands the earlier impact statement with specific author-participant bias, judge-family bias and simulation boundaries. Privacy discussion also distinguishes o4-mini's privacy/performance tradeoff.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/data repository link, precise model identifiers and dates, interaction and judge-calibration details, and detailed Telehealth expert guidelines. However, Appendix A omits the Color Puzzle lookup rules supplied in v2, despite retaining text referring to that table. The shared agent prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning relative to test-time compute and hybrid reasoning, with citations to Snell, Llama-Nemotron, Qwen3, the newly evaluated reasoning models and BLEU. VQA and several jailbreak citations disappear. The established comparison with single-agent benchmarks and multi-agent frameworks remains.

P1.justification: V3 revises selected abstract, introduction and analysis passages, moves cognitive-science background into Related Work, and relocates detailed model descriptions to Appendix A. It reorganizes limitations and appendix headings, while preserving the main section sequence and much of the existing prose.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a predominantly single-column layout and introduces colored model groups in tables. V3 expands the error chart, merges conversation-length and redesigned privacy plots, and adds efficiency, ablation and trajectory displays. The capability chart and Color Puzzle lookup display disappear.

improvement.justification: The new ablations and efficiency analysis improve diagnostic value, while explicit human and judge bias limitations better qualify the findings. However, v3 removes the Color Puzzle rules and introduces an unexplained discrepancy between o4-mini's reported 53.98% overall PSR and the 43.8% average of its displayed puzzle scores under the stated averaging rule. These substantive gains and unresolved reproducibility and reporting problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
